title: Active Directory Excessive Permissions / ACL Misconfiguration
description: Excessive or misconfigured Access Control Entries on Active Directory objects (such as GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDacl, WriteOwner, or the right to reset passwords) allow lower-privileged principals to take control of higher-privileged users, groups, or computers. Chains of such delegated rights frequently create unintended paths from a standard user to Domain Admin. Over-permissive group nesting and stale privileged memberships compound the risk.
businessImpact: Critical --- abusable permission chains can lead to takeover of privileged accounts and complete compromise of the directory.
remediation:
- Enforce least privilege and regularly review ACLs on users, groups, OUs, and the domain root.
- Remove dangerous rights (WriteDacl, WriteOwner, GenericAll) granted to non-administrative principals.
- Flatten and review group nesting; remove stale members of privileged groups.
- Use tiered administration and a dedicated admin forest/model for Tier 0 assets.
- Continuously map attack paths (e.g., with BloodHound) and remediate the shortest paths to Tier 0.
